chunks: And from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say frequently: Al-Taymī and Al-ʿAdawī would gather in the presence of Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله while he was reciting “Indeed, We sent it down” with humility and weeping, and they would say: How intense is your tenderness for this surah.

So Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله would say: Because of what my eye has seen, what my heart has comprehended, and what the heart of this one will see after me. So they would say: And what is it that you saw, and what is it that he will see?
He said: Then he would write for them in the dust: “The angels and the Spirit descend therein, by the permission of their Lord, with every affair.”

He said: Then he would say: Does anything remain after His, Mighty and Majestic, saying, “with every affair”? They would say: No. Then he would say: Do you know to whom that is sent down? They would say: To you, O Rasūl Allāh. He would say: Yes.

Then he would say: Will Laylat al-Qadr exist after me? They would say: Yes. He said: Then he would say: Will that affair descend in it? They would say: Yes. He said: Then he would say: To whom? They would say: We do not know. Then he would take hold of my head and say: If you do not know, then know: it is this one after me.
He said: So indeed they both came to recognize that night after Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله because of the intensity of the dread that entered into them.

key_terms.إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ: the opening words of Sūrat al-Qadr, cited here as the subject of reflection
key_terms.التَّيْمِيُّ: the man from Banū Taym, referring here to a specific companion lineage
key_terms.الرُّعْبِ: the dread or awe that entered them after this clarification
key_terms.الْعَدَوِيُّ: the man from Banū ʿAdī, referring here to a specific companion lineage
key_terms.تَنَزَّلُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ وَالرُّوحُ: the descent of the angels and the Spirit during Laylat al-Qadr
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ: the Night of Decree, which the narration presents as continuing after the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.مِنْ كُلِّ أَمْرٍ: with every affair; indicating comprehensiveness of what is sent down

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith use Sūrat al-Qadr to indicate the authority of ʿAlī عليه السلام after the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله?
ai.summary: This narration explains the significance of Sūrat al-Qadr as indicating that the descent of the angels and the Spirit with every affair continues after the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله. In the text, Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله identifies ʿAlī عليه السلام as the one to whom that affair descends after him, presenting the verse as proof of continuing divine authority and knowledge after the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله.

en.hubeali:
And, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘It was so that Aliasws was frequently saying: ‘There would not gather (from the Clan of) Al-Taymi (Abu Bakr) and (from the Clan of) Al-Adwy (Umar) in the presence of Rasool-Allahsaww and hesaww recited [97:1] We have indeed revealed this Chapter 97) with humbleness and crying, so they would both be saying: ‘How intense is youras soft-heartedness for this Chapter!’

So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was saying: ‘(It is) due to what my eyes see, and my<sup>saww</sup> heart feels, and due to what the heart of this one<sup>asws</sup> would see from after me<sup>saww</sup>’. So they were both saying, ‘What is that which your<sup>saww</sup> heart is seeing, and what is that which his<sup>asws</sup> heart would see?’
Heasws said: ‘So hesaww wrote for them both in the sand [97:4] Therein come down the angels and the Spirit by Allah's permission, on every affair’.

Heasws said: ‘Then hesaww was saying: ‘Does there remain anything after Hisazwj Words every affair?’ So they were both saying, ‘No’. So hesaww was saying: ‘Do you two know who they descend upon with that?’ So they were saying, ‘Yousaww, O Rasool-Allahsaww!’. So hesaww was saying: ‘Yes’.

So hesaww was saying: ‘Would there happen to be a Night of Pre-determination (Laylat Al-Qadr) (to come) after mesaww?’ So they both were saying, ‘Yes’. So hesaww was saying: ‘So would that affair be descending during it?’ So they were saying, ‘Yes’. So hesaww was saying: ‘Unto whom?’ So they were saying, ‘We don’t know’. So hesaww grabbed myasws head and hesaww was saying: ‘If you don’t know, so know, it is this oneasws, from after mesaww’.
Heasws said: ‘So it was such that they both (the two from the Clans of Taymi and Adwy) recognised that night (Laylat Al-Qadr) from the intensity of what entered into them from the awe’.
en.sarwar: 4. Through the same chain of narrators it is narrated from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.

“Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) would say, “We revealed the Quran on the Night of Destiny ([97:1] Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, has certainly said the truth has reveal the Holy Quran on the Night of Determination. “Would that you knew what the Night of Destiny is! [97:2]” the Messenger of Allah said, “I do not know.”

Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, said, “(Worship) on the Night of Destiny is better than (worship) for a thousand months (that are other than the Night of Determinatio).” [97:3] He asked the Messenger of Allah, “Do you know why it is better than a thousand nights?” the Messenger of Allah said, “No, I do not know.”
He said, “It is because on that Night the angels and the Spirit come down by the permission of their Lord for all matters.

When Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, would grant permission for a matter it means that He has agreed.” “This Night is all peace until the break of dawn.” [97:5] He says, “O Muhammad, My angels salute you and My spirit with peaceful greetings from beginning of the time they come down until dawn of that night. Then He has said in another part of His book, “Guard yourselves against discord among yourselves so that it will not mislead anyone of you, especially the unjust, and know that God’s retribution is most severe.” [8:25] It is about the Night of Determination. He has also said in His book, “Muhammad is only a Messenger. There lived other Messengers before him. Should (Muhammad) die or be slain, would you then turn back to your pre-Islamic behavior? Whoever does so can cause no harm to God. God will reward those who give thanks.” [3:144] In the verse He has said that when Muhammad will die the opposition to the command of Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, will say , “The Night of Determination has gone along with the Messenger of Allah.” This is the first clamity that has befallen them exclusively. With this they returned back to their old ways. Had they not said so, it would have been necessary to believe that Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, has His commands on that Night. Once they would affirm and acknowledge the command (delegation of Divine authority) it would have become necessary to believe in the existence of the man who possesses Divine authority.”
